mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior month reduces discount rates applied to corporate earnings forecasts, lowering the present value of future cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns in the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite elevated FEDFUNDS, or discount rate sensitivity (MRW) estimates are below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 50,000 jobs signals labor market resilience that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 50,000 in the prior month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns underperform a 5-day moving average baseline with a p-value < 0.05 in a two-tailed test.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% indicates weakening supply-side constraints that, when combined with elevated consumer demand (GDPC1), amplifies upward pressure on equity valuations and produces positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 2% in the prior month
failure_condition: No significant correlation between INDPRO decline and SPX 20-day returns (Spearman's rho < 0.2) after controlling for CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 303 suggests deflationary pressures that reduce expected inflation premia and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls by 1% in the prior month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.10) in a one-tailed test.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate remains persistently below 3% during a month, it reflects policy accommodation that lowers real borrowing costs and supports equity risk premiums, producing positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS stays below 3% for the prior 4 weeks
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns underperform a 5-day moving average baseline with a p-value < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% triggers a confidence surge among equity investors, generating positive 60-day forward returns even when broader economic indicators are neutral.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% in the prior month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant deviation from zero (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (HOUST) above 1,400 indicate healthy consumer demand that, when sustained, elevates growth expectations and drives positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds 1,400 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite sustained HOUST growth (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in supply-side indicators (RSAFS > 700,000) coinciding with a decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL < 305) suggests successful supply-chain normalization that reduces cost pressures and supports positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls by 2% while RSAFS increases by 20% in the prior month
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 60 days (p > 0.05) after controlling for FEDFUNDS and UNRATE.
